archetypes.name: Grounded Navigator
archetypes.description: You're secure in yourself and your relationships. You can be close without losing yourself, and independent without pushing others away.
archetypes.expandedDescription: You have a secure foundation in relationships. You're comfortable with both closeness and independence, and you can navigate emotional intensity without becoming overwhelmed or shutting down. You trust that people who love you will stay, and you're able to be authentic without excessive fear of rejection. Your relationships tend to be stable and satisfying. While you're not immune to relationship challenges, you have the internal resources to work through them.
archetypes.shadowSide: You may become complacent, assuming security is a ceiling rather than a foundation for exploration.
archetypes.growthPath: Keep choosing growth even when comfortable.

archetypes.name: Emotional Enthusiast
archetypes.description: You feel everything intensely and wear your heart on your sleeve. You want deep connection and aren't afraid to show how much you care.
archetypes.expandedDescription: You feel everything intensely. Your emotions are vivid, powerful, and sometimes overwhelming. In relationships, you want deep connection and you're not afraid to show how much you care. You may worry about being abandoned or rejected, and you need reassurance that you matter. Your passion is a gift—you bring aliveness, enthusiasm, and emotional depth to relationships.
archetypes.shadowSide: You may confuse intensity with intimacy, leading to overwhelming experiences that aren't necessarily connecting.
archetypes.growthPath: Develop your capacity to soothe yourself when anxious, rather than always seeking external reassurance.

archetypes.name: Lone Wolf
archetypes.description: You value independence and self-sufficiency. You protect yourself by maintaining distance and staying in control.
archetypes.expandedDescription: You value independence and self-sufficiency above almost everything. You're most comfortable when you're in control and when you maintain some emotional distance. Vulnerability feels threatening, so you protect yourself by not needing anyone too much. Your strength is your self-reliance—you're calm under pressure and you respect boundaries.
archetypes.shadowSide: The walls that protect you also isolate you. You may miss out on deep connection by defending against it.
archetypes.growthPath: Allow safe vulnerability; connection doesn't mean engulfment.
archetypes.strengths: Self-reliant, calm under pressure, respectful of boundaries

archetypes.name: Mystery Mosaic
archetypes.description: Your early experiences were confusing. You may swing between wanting closeness and needing distance.
archetypes.expandedDescription: Your early experiences taught you that caregivers could be both the source of comfort and the source of fear. This created confusion about how to be close to others. You may swing between desperately wanting closeness and needing to push it away. Your emotions and relationships may feel unpredictable, even to you. Despite this, you have profound capacity for growth and resilience.
archetypes.shadowSide: Unpredictable patterns can create confusion for yourself and others.
archetypes.growthPath: With support, develop more stable patterns and learn to trust both yourself and others.
archetypes.strengths: Resilient, adaptable, deep capacity for growth

archetypes.name: Heartfelt Defender
archetypes.description: You show the world a polished version of yourself while hiding the messy parts. You achieve to feel worthy.
archetypes.expandedDescription: You show the world a polished, competent version of yourself while keeping the messy, vulnerable parts hidden. You achieve, perform, and give to feel worthy of love. Deep down, you fear that if people saw the real you—with all your needs, flaws, and struggles—they would leave. So you hide. You're likely successful, well-liked, and exhausted.
archetypes.shadowSide: Hiding your true self leads to exhaustion and feeling unlovable without performance.
archetypes.growthPath: Let the mask crack; you're lovable without performing. Reveal small truths and discover that people stay.

archetypes.name: Chill Conductor
archetypes.description: You live in your head and observe life from a slight distance. You're brilliant at understanding but struggle to feel.
archetypes.expandedDescription: You live in your head and observe the world from a slight distance. You're brilliant at analyzing, understanding, and explaining, but you struggle to drop into your body and actually feel. Emotions are interesting to you intellectually, but experiencing them fully feels threatening. Your strength is your objectivity and insight.
archetypes.shadowSide: The observer position protects you, but it also keeps you from fully living.
archetypes.growthPath: Practice dropping from head to body—noticing sensations, feelings, aliveness.

archetypes.name: Passionate Pilgrim
archetypes.description: You long to belong completely to someone. You'll do almost anything to prove your devotion and avoid abandonment.
archetypes.expandedDescription: You have a deep desire to feel chosen and valued. You want relationships where commitment is clear and where you don’t have to question whether someone will stay. Your dedication, consistency, and willingness to show up fully are genuine strengths. At the same time, you sometimes look to others to create a sense of security that can only take root from within.
archetypes.shadowSide: You may seek security through devotion rather than building it within yourself.
archetypes.growthPath: Build a steadier inner foundation so your worth doesn't depend on others' reassurance.
archetypes.strengths: Devoted, loyal, passionate, willing to grow

archetypes.name: Independent Icon
archetypes.description: You pride yourself on needing no one. You're powerful, self-contained, and possibly lonely without knowing it.
archetypes.expandedDescription: You pride yourself on needing no one. You're powerful, self-sufficient, and possibly lonely without fully realizing it. You may dismiss others' needs as weakness and see your own lack of need as strength. Your competence and independence are real—but so is your defended position.
archetypes.shadowSide: Dismissing needs isn't the same as transcending them. You may be lonely without realizing it.
archetypes.growthPath: Allow yourself to need someone. It doesn't destroy you—it makes you human.

archetypes.name: The Shrinker
archetypes.description: You tend to withdraw and become smaller when things get intense.
archetypes.expandedDescription: As a subtype of the Mystery Mosaic, you tend to manage the confusion of intimacy by shrinking—becoming quieter, smaller, or trying to disappear. This protects you from potential conflict or rejection, but also prevents you from being fully seen and supported.
archetypes.shadowSide: Making yourself small keeps you safe but invisible.
archetypes.growthPath: Practice taking up space and letting yourself be seen, even when it feels risky.

archetypes.name: The Performer
archetypes.description: You use achievement and competence to mask your insecurities.
archetypes.expandedDescription: As a subtype of the Heartfelt Defender, you rely heavily on performance—being the best, the most helpful, or the most competent—to feel secure. You worry that without your achievements, you wouldn't be enough.
archetypes.shadowSide: Your self-worth becomes tied entirely to what you do, rather than who you are.
archetypes.growthPath: Separate your worth from your work. Practice 'being' rather than 'doing'.
